# Character Sheet Generation

## Purpose

Turn a locked character identity into reference sheets drawn in the comic's
own style. Pages attach these sheets as identity references, so each page
request points at the same drawing of the character and does not have to
describe them again from text.

## Use When

- A character file is ready and has no visual masters yet.
- A new outfit or a new identity version needs its own sheet.
- An existing sheet is too weak to hold identity: face in shadow, one view
  only, wrong drawing style.
- A recurring secondary character has started to change between pages.

## Inputs

- `production/characters/<CHAR_ID>/character.yaml` and `wardrobe.yaml`.
- The approved look master (`project.style.look_refs`) and
  `production/style/style-block.txt`.
- Identity photographs or costume references the user supplied, already
  registered by `reference-ingestion`.
- Provider capabilities from `manifests/image-providers.json`.

## Process

1. Check the preconditions. The character file has distinguishing features
   and an adjacency list, the style block is written, and a look master is
   approved. Without an approved look there is no style to draw the sheet
   in, and `compile-prompts.js` refuses the sheet. Stop and finish the look
   first.
2. Plan the set by role. A protagonist or antagonist gets a turnaround
   (front, three-quarter, profile, back, full figure), an expression sheet
   with the five or six expressions the script calls for, and one wardrobe
   sheet per outfit beyond the default. A recurring secondary character gets
   at least a turnaround. Background characters get nothing.
3. Compile one package per sheet, the turnaround first:
   `node scripts/compile-prompts.js --asset <CHAR_ID> --sheet turnaround --root <workspace>`.
   The other kinds are `expressions` (`--expressions a,b,c` replaces the
   default list: neutral, wary, angry, afraid, in pain, relieved),
   `wardrobe` (`--outfit <WARD_ID>`, default the character's
   `default_wardrobe`), and `detail` with `--subject "<text>"` for a close
   study of one feature. The script writes
   `characters/<CHAR_ID>/refs/prompts/<provider>.<kind>.yaml`, an
   asset-scoped package (`page: null`, `asset: <CHAR_ID>`, id
   `PP_<CHAR_ID>_<PROVIDER>-<TAG>`, with TAG `TURN`, `EXPR`, `WARD`, or
   `DETAIL`). A wardrobe package carries its outfit in the file name and
   the ID (`<provider>.wardrobe.WARD_MARA_OILSKIN.yaml`,
   `...-WARD-OILSKIN`), and a detail package a slug of its subject
   (`<provider>.detail.torn-left-cuff.yaml`, `...-DETAIL-TORN_LEFT_CUFF`).
   The prompt opens with the style block verbatim and takes its
   subject from `prompt_summary`, the `description` fields,
   `distinguishing_features`, and the outfit entry, plus one line for each
   character in `visually_adjacent_to` that states the difference. The
   look master is attached with role `style`. Expression and wardrobe
   sheets also attach the character's approved identity master with role
   `identity`, so approve the turnaround before compiling them. Without an
   approved one the script still compiles and notes that the sheet is drawn
   from the written description only. Each outfit and each detail subject
   has its own package file, so every sheet of a character can be compiled
   before the first is generated.
4. Read the brief the script wrote. It asks for sheet conditions and
   nothing else: plain light background, even light, no cast shadow across
   the face, neutral stance, every figure at the same scale with feet on
   one baseline, heads the same size across an expression sheet. Dramatic
   lighting belongs on the pages. A sheet lit like a scene hides the
   features and teaches every later page the same shadow. When the wording
   about the character is wrong, correct the character file and compile
   again. Do not edit the compiled `prompt`.
5. Dry-run first:
   `node scripts/generate-assets.js --asset <CHAR_ID> --root <workspace>`
   runs every sheet package compiled for the character, and
   `--package <file>` runs one. Read the `GEN_*.request.json` it writes,
   confirm the cost, then repeat with `--live --yes`.
6. Open every returned file. Check that it is a drawing in the look's
   style: same line, same black placement, same degree of simplification as
   the look master. A grayscale portrait is not a stylized drawing, however
   good the likeness, and is rejected. The identity anchors have to survive
   the simplification.
7. Check agreement across views. The face at three-quarter and in profile
   is the same person as the front view. Sided features sit on the correct
   side in every view. Hands, cuffs, and accessories match the outfit.
8. Put the sheet next to the sheets of every character in
   `visually_adjacent_to`. Shrunk to panel size, the two must still be
   told apart at a glance. If they cannot, the design goes back to
   `character-consistency`.
9. Promote the pick. Generation saves each candidate as
   `<CHAR_ID>_<TAG>_V##` (for example `CHAR_MARA_TURN_V01.png`, or
   `CHAR_MARA_WARD_OILSKIN_V01.png` and
   `CHAR_MARA_DETAIL_TORN_LEFT_CUFF_V01.png` for an outfit and a detail)
   under `production/characters/<CHAR_ID>/refs/`, always the next free
   version and never under a `_MASTER` name. Each attempt has its
   generation record and request file under
   `production/generations/<CHAR_ID>/`. Submit the selected candidate for
   review under its candidate name.
10. Record approval per reference. The user approves each sheet
    individually. For each approved one run
    `node scripts/approve-asset.js --candidate <CHAR_ID>_<TAG>_V## --root production`.
    It copies the candidate to `<CHAR_ID>_<TAG>_MASTER_V##` with the same
    version (for example `CHAR_MARA_TURN_MASTER_V01`), registers it in
    `production/references/manifest.yaml` with `status: approved`,
    `approved_by`, `approved_at`, its generation record, and `default_role`
    (`identity`, or `wardrobe` for an outfit sheet), and adds the asset ID
    to `character.references` and, for an outfit sheet, to the outfit's
    `references`. Reuse approvals that exist and ask only about sheets that
    are new.
11. Correct a sheet by making the next version. Approve the new candidate
    with `approve-asset.js --supersede`: the old asset becomes `superseded`
    and its file stays on disk.

## Outputs

- Sheet packages under `production/characters/<CHAR_ID>/refs/prompts/`
  (`prompt-package` schema).
- Sheet images under `production/characters/<CHAR_ID>/refs/`.
- Registry entries in `production/references/manifest.yaml`, with status and
  approval per asset.
- One generation record per image (`generation-record` schema).
- Updated `references` lists in `character.yaml` and `wardrobe.yaml`.

## Quality Bar

- Every sheet is drawn in the look master's style; none is a photograph or
  a grayscale render.
- The face is readable and the same person in every view and expression.
- Plain background, even light, consistent scale.
- Every outfit in `wardrobe.yaml` that appears on a page has a sheet or is
  covered by the turnaround.
- Every recurring secondary character has at least a turnaround.
- Every sheet has a registry entry, a status, and a generation record.
  Reference plans cite only assets with `status: approved`.

## Common Failure Modes

- Scene lighting on a sheet. Half the face is black, and every page that
  attaches it inherits a character with half a face.
- A photoreal or grayscale portrait accepted as the master. Pages then
  drift toward photographic rendering around that one character.
- A strong front view whose profile belongs to someone else.
- Mirrored anchors: the torn cuff on the left arm in one view and the right
  in the next.
- Expression sheets where each face changes proportions, so the "angry"
  head is effectively a second character.
- Regenerating the whole set when one view failed.
- No sheet for the deckhand who appears on six pages, because he is "only
  secondary".
- Citing a draft sheet from a reference plan before anyone approved it.

## Notes

Generation itself follows `image-generation`: dry run, cost confirmation,
one record per file. Replacing a master means rechecking every reference
plan and prompt package that cited the old version. Approval rules are in
`rules/common/approval-policy.md`.
